report: Reviewed the complete claim, sole ordinary validate.rs implementation association, and all three ordinary annotated tests; no TODO/N/A entries or deferred prerequisites exist. Independently confirmed exact byte equality of validate.rs, envelopes.rs, and language.rs against the historical input, reconstructing its line arrays with newline joins. The prior rationale remains supported by current source: Model::check builds edges only from permitted Invokes effects, resolves prohibition targets separately, and searches every reachable edge from each applicable implementation. Seeding two-method paths excludes zero-edge reachability; checking the target before the seen-set guard handles direct and recursive hits, while the seen set terminates cycles. targets includes known descendant overrides. Diagnostics join the actual traversed method sequence. The envelopes test asserts the full Root -> Helper -> Leaf rejection path and uses captured valid helper assertions to verify removing the permitted first edge eliminates rejection. Its direct-permission assertions also distinguish graph reachability from direct permission. The virtual-dispatch test requires exactly two errors and each complete Caller -> override -> body sequence; the recursive-graph test asserts no diagnostics for a self-cycle with an unreachable prohibited body. Together these meaningful positive/negative assertions and source reasoning cover permitted nonempty reachability, conservative branches, cycle termination, and offending sequence identification; no isolated extra assertion is required for the queue initialization. Captured parse/valid/check fixture helpers establish that these calls parse actual models and validate them. I ran review start, review read, source inspection and exact baseline comparison, and review record; I did not execute behavioral tests or builds. The coordinator separately reports 321 functional tests passing and a successful root cargo build; that execution is not my evidence of having run them. No edits are needed.
